layers.rule: Ids are minted once, opaque, and never derived from or parsed for names. Everything else refers to them.
Time-dependent facts about identities. Every record carries a Validity and a Provenance. History is added, never overwritten.
Bytes are identity; paths and URLs are locations of bytes at a time. Attribution is a judgement about an artifact, never a property of it.
What a document (or a person, or a legacy file) said, kept for ever, including what lost.
A persistent, rule-named choice between observations. Losers are referenced, not removed.
A projection of the latest effective reconciliation. Never the only record of what sources said.
Attach to records of any layer without collapsing them.

RelationshipStatus.note: How firmly the estate-wine link is held, independent of its role.

BoundKind.note: NO_LATER_THAN and NO_EARLIER_THAN are inclusive: 'sheets listed from 2016' makes a start NO_LATER_THAN vintage 2016.

BoundAxis.note: Wine facts change by vintage ('from the 2008 vintage'), institutional facts by calendar date ('juin 1973'). A bound says which.

CanonicalStatus.note: LEGACY_UNSOURCED, not MANUAL_UNSOURCED, for today's values without provenance: field-src.js says such a field 'was entered by hand or predates the reader', so 'manual' cannot be asserted. MANUAL_UNSOURCED is for values entered by hand from Phase 4 on.

ReconciliationRule.note: The two LEGACY_ rules name what read-fiches.py did, so the history of today's winners is honest; no new reconciliation may use them.

WineType.note: What kind of wine it is. Independent of rank: Myosotis (WHITE_DRY) is a first wine, Les Tourelles (WHITE_SWEET) a third, Les Murets rouge (RED) unranked as far as any source says.

RankTier.note: Where a claimant places a wine in a range. FIRST is the grand vin / premier vin; ABOVE_FIRST a cuvee placed above it (Mangot: "in truth it is the superior cuvee"); UNRANKED is an explicit statement that no rank applies (Le Rey: "do not represent ... first and second label"); UNKNOWN is no statement. There is no OTHER: a wine nobody ranks has no rank assertion.

RankScope.note: The range a rank is within: the estate's whole range, or its range of one WineType (Caillou: Myosotis FIRST and Les Murets blanc SECOND within WHITE_DRY).

Claimant.note: Who asserts a rank. Ranks are claims: Mangot's cuvee is SECOND for the classification authorities and ABOVE_FIRST in the producer's and press's words.

RelationshipKind.note: What links a wine to an estate. Several may hold at once (Les Terrasses: from the estate's younger vines, created by the Vignobles K team). A wine on an estate's site is not thereby the estate's (Chateau Langlet on Latour-Martillac's site).

DescriptorKind.note: How a wine is made or selected - never a rank. "Selection parcellaire" names Lacroix-Martillac and also describes vat work at dozens of estates; single-variety is derived from the blend, not stored.

EditionStatus.note: Saint-Emilion 2006 was annulled ("classement annule depuis", Grand Corbin-Despagne).

ArtifactDateKind.note: 93 % of harvested PDFs carry a metadata date, 70 % an upload-path date: the anchor for "today" and "now" in a document.

ArtifactRelationKind.note: Between artifacts, always as a candidate with its evidence; never equivalence of content (Murmure 2018: two French revisions, 14.5 % and 14 %; the English, 14 %).

SourceRelationKind.note: 25 domains serve several target estates; 31 sites moved domain.

ExtractionStatus.note: 374 image-only PDFs exist before any OCR; the model must not need their text.

SubjectStatus.note: Whose statement an observation is, inside a document that may cover several estates.

Wine.identity: minted opaque id; the grand vin is a Wine
Wine.note: Identity apart from name, type apart from rank. The grand vin is a Wine.

Vintage.identity: composite (wine, label): label is a year or 'NV'

Party.note: Legal identifiers (SIRET, RCS) may be attached when established; legal notices themselves stay observations about the site publisher.

NameRecord.note: context: the market or channel a name is used in (Desmirail: Initial de Desmirail "aussi distribue sous le nom de Origine de Desmirail").

EstateWineRelationship.note: One record per kind of link; validity per record.

ClassificationMembership.note: The subject is the classified Wine, not the Estate: Graves classifies per colour, Crus Artisans per appellation (Moutte Blanc). 'The estate is classified' is a derived view.

EditorialCollectionMembership.note: The dashboard's editorial groupings (Pomerol, Libournais, Côtes, Graves & Entre-Deux-Mers, Médoc beyond the lists). Never a classification.

Artifact.identity: minted opaque id; equality by digest
Artifact.note: At least one digest is required. Two artifacts with a digest in common are one artifact. Bytes overwritten before Phase 4 survive only as a sha1 from the manifest: bytes_available false.

Placement.note: One path, many artifacts over time: one Placement per (locator, artifact). An artifact may be null when the path is known and the bytes are not (the 123 provenance failures).

Attribution.note: A judgement of what an artifact concerns; role is now a RankTier claim, null when unknown.

LegacyDocumentReference.note: How a bare filename cited by field-src.js, cuvee-src.js or a record's src stays resolvable: to the candidate placements, never silently to one.

EvidenceLink.note: Points from the immutable evidence store into the new identities. The store is not rewritten; the link is built beside it.

Observation.identity: minted opaque id; unique on (artifact, locus, subject, field, extractor)
Observation.note: raw_label and lang as printed; asserted_at anchors "today", "now", "currently" to the document's date (an ArtifactDate), distinct from when the fact holds (validity of the state it supports) and from when it was retrieved.

CanonicalValue.note: lang: the language of a canonical text value; as_of: the date a time-dependent value (vineyard area, owner) is known to hold.

Provenance.note: One shape for every layer. Kinds named LEGACY_* say exactly what is known about a pre-migration value and no more.

RankAssertion.note: A claimant's statement of where a wine stands in a range, in time.

RankAbsence.note: A statement that a rank is empty - for good, or for one vintage (Corbin 2022: "no second wine was produced this year").

WineDescriptor.note: How a wine is made or selected, kept apart from its rank.

SourceEstateRelationship.note: A source serving or mentioning an estate. Never identity: a group site serves several estates.

ArtifactDate.note: Candidate dates of a document, several per artifact, each with how it is known.

ArtifactRelation.note: Language versions, revisions, family membership - candidates, never content equivalence.

DocumentFamily.note: A derived grouping of one source's documents that share a layout (849 families; none shared across domains; 27 span languages). An extraction aid, not domain truth.

Translation.note: A derived text in another language. Never an observation, never evidence of equivalence.

migrations.name: Freeze
migrations.does: Tag the last pre-migration commit; record hashes of every canonical file, the manifest and the evidence index; snapshot the semantics (key shapes, role vocabularies, sparse-id rule, '—' meaning) as tests.

migrations.name: Stable identities
migrations.does: Mint ids for estates, other wines, sources, parties; build IdentityMap from every legacy key: full-record ids, name-derived compact ids, (estate, slug) wine keys, (estate, display name) wine references used by evidence target_wine.

migrations.name: Estate/Wine split
migrations.does: Mint one grand-vin Wine per estate with a legacy grand-vin record; EstateWineRelationship for it and for every BDX_CUVEE_WINES wine; map 'estate|vintage' keys to (grand-vin Wine, vintage) through IdentityMap.
migrations.reverse: drop relationships and minted grand-vin wines

migrations.name: Roles and time
migrations.does: RoleAssignment from legacy roles (second -> SECOND_WINE; other -> UNKNOWN with legacy_term 'other'); RoleAbsence from second '—'; ClassificationMembership on wines from the estate files and, separately, from the Phase 3.0 universe as AUTHORITATIVE_SOURCE statements; Ownership from owner strings (a stated year kept at YEAR precision, else UNKNOWN); every bound UNKNOWN unless a source states it.

migrations.name: Artifact identity
migrations.does: Artifacts by digest from the manifest (sha1) and the evidence (sha256), joined where both are known for the same bytes; Locators and Placements from every manifest row, one per (path, digest), ordered by first appearance; Placement MISSING/NAME_MISMATCH for the 123 provenance failures; LegacyDocumentReference for every basename in field-src.js, cuvee-src.js, cellar/terroir/plantings src.

migrations.name: Observations
migrations.does: Observations from legacy canonical values (one per value, provenance LEGACY_FIELD_SOURCE / LEGACY_RECORD_SOURCE / LEGACY_AMBIGUOUS_SOURCE / LEGACY_UNSOURCED, exactly as known); EvidenceLinks for v4/v5 rows (v1-v3 rows stay interpretable through IdentityMap but are not linked to bytes they never hashed); Attributions LEGACY from manifest rows; ArtifactAssessments LEGACY.

migrations.name: Reconciliation
migrations.does: One Reconciliation per (subject, field) with a legacy value: rule LEGACY_NEVER_OVERWRITE, status LEGACY_RETAINED, candidates = every observation for it; new document observations (re-extraction under a provenance-safe extractor) enter as candidates and open CONFLICT_OPEN where they disagree.

migrations.name: Canonical projection
migrations.does: Generate CanonicalValues from reconciliations, and from them byte-identical regenerations of today's data files; any difference is a migration defect, not a correction.
migrations.reverse: stop projecting; the hand-maintained files are still the app's input

migrations.name: Consumers
migrations.does: Point the app, readers and tools at the projections and the new layers, one consumer at a time, each behind a switch; readers write Observations and Attributions PROPOSED, never canonical files.
migrations.reverse: flip the consumer's switch back; the old files are still generated

migrations.name: Retirement
migrations.does: After a full release on the new layers, archive (tag) and stop generating obsolete structures; the identity maps and legacy references stay for ever.

invariants.I1: Every current estate remains addressable (each of the 470 canonical estate keys resolves to one stable Estate).
invariants.I2: Every historical estate id remains resolvable (IdentityMap holds every legacy key ever used: data files, manifest estate, evidence ctx.estate and target_estate).
invariants.I3: Every current wine remains addressable (each grand vin and each BDX_CUVEE_WINES entry resolves to one Wine).
invariants.I4: Grand vins become Wine entities without changing what they denote: every legacy 'estate|vintage' key maps to exactly one (Wine, Vintage) of that estate's grand-vin Wine.
invariants.I5: No wine is silently assigned a role: every RoleAssignment has a provenance, and legacy 'other' becomes UNKNOWN with legacy_term 'other', never OTHER_CUVEE.
invariants.I6: UNKNOWN role is representable and used where a wine's membership is known and its role is not.
invariants.I7: Historical relationships do not overwrite current ones: records are added with validity; none is updated in place.
invariants.I8: Evidence decisions remain interpretable: every v1-v5 row's estate and target_estate resolve through IdentityMap; target_wine resolves through the (estate, display name) wine map.
invariants.I9: Artifact hashes remain unchanged: digests are copied, never recomputed over different bytes.
invariants.I10: Historical file versions remain distinguishable: one Placement per (path, digest); the 204 multi-version paths keep every version.
invariants.I11: Losing observations remain recoverable: every Reconciliation lists all candidates; no observation is deleted.
invariants.I12: Canonical values retain provenance where provenance exists: field-level where field-src names a uniquely resolvable document, ambiguous-candidates where it does not.
invariants.I13: Unsourced values are not given fabricated provenance: a record-level src is never promoted to field provenance (Badette 2020 oak); values without field provenance are LEGACY_RECORD_SOURCE_ONLY or LEGACY_UNSOURCED.
invariants.I14: Multi-estate documents remain multi-estate capable: Attribution is many per artifact.
invariants.I15: Shared sources do not imply shared estate identity: Source and Estate are linked only through Placement and Attribution, never by identity.
invariants.I16: Proposals remain separate from canonical values: proposals.jsonl and attribution-candidates.jsonl become PROPOSED Attributions or nothing; no migration step reads them into state or canonical layers.
invariants.I17: The 908 unattributed documents remain representable: an Artifact with no ACCEPTED or LEGACY Attribution, and an explicit UNATTRIBUTED one where it was examined.
invariants.I18: The 123 unreadable files remain representable: Placements MISSING (103) or NAME_MISMATCH (20) with no artifact, each with an EXTRACTION_FAILURE or SOURCE_FAILURE finding.
invariants.I19: Existing v1-v5 evidence is not rewritten: data/evidence/ is byte-identical before and after every migration step.
invariants.I20: No migration step requires a complete wine universe: absence of a RoleAssignment is UNKNOWN; nothing waits for the 385 estates' wines.
invariants.I21: The authoritative universe stays a separate statement layer (AUTHORITATIVE_SOURCE provenance); reaching state or canonical layers only through reconciliation.
invariants.I22: A legacy basename never resolves by first match: a LegacyDocumentReference with more than one candidate stays AMBIGUOUS until a reviewed decision.

open_decisions.D1: What the estate-level `blend` in the estate files and plantings.js denotes, per estate: vineyard plantings or the grand vin's usual assemblage. The model holds both kinds of observation; which one each legacy value is needs domain review (memory: 'a vineyard label can carry the assemblage').
open_decisions.D2: Whether Haut-Bages Averous -> Echo de Lynch-Bages is one wine renamed or a succession of two wines. The estate's 'change d'identité pour devenir' supports both; the model records SUCCEEDED_BY with certainty UNRESOLVED until decided.
open_decisions.D3: The storage and format of the normalized layers (files, SQLite, other). Phase 4.
open_decisions.D4: The concrete syntax of minted ids. The rules are fixed (opaque, minted once, never parsed); the spelling is Phase 4's.
open_decisions.D5: Reconciliation policy for new conflicts: the priority between an estate's own sheet and its trade copy, between language versions of one sheet (Badette EN 80 / FR 50; Chevalier EN '16-20' / FR '18'), between a document and the authoritative universe. Until set, conflicts stay CONFLICT_OPEN and the legacy value is retained.
open_decisions.D6: The classification of the 85 distinct manifest `how` texts into retrieval method, attribution method, or both. Mechanical but a judgement; unclassified texts migrate verbatim as LEGACY_UNKNOWN.
open_decisions.D7: How the app consumes the new layers in M8: regenerated files of today's shape, or a new loader. The projection must exist either way.
open_decisions.D8: Names for classified wines no source names (the classified whites of Bouscaut, Carbonnieux, Latour-Martillac and Malartic-Lagravière): migrate with name_status UNKNOWN, or research them first. Not a blocker (I20).

identity_change_evidence.RENAMED: the source names one wine as the continuing subject under a new name (Haut-Bailly: "La Parde ... se voit renommer"; Lynch-Bages EN: "a new identity was given to the second wine")
identity_change_evidence.SUCCEEDED_BY: the source presents the new wine as replacing a discontinued one, without continuity of the wine
identity_change_evidence.SPLIT_FROM: one wine (or estate) becomes two, with dated statements for both
identity_change_evidence.MERGED_INTO: two become one, with a dated statement (La Tour Haut-Brion 2006)
identity_change_evidence.POSSIBLY_SAME: same name, no statement either way (Bellevue, La Commanderie)
identity_change_evidence.NEW_UNRELATED: no transition record at all: absence of evidence is not a transition
